title: Business broker
summary: Represents sellers, markets businesses and runs the sale process.
does: Prepares the listing, teaser and CIM
Screens buyers and manages confidentiality agreements
Runs the process and relays offers
Keeps the deal moving to closing
doesNot: Represent you as the buyer (usually)
Verify the seller's numbers for you
Give you legal, tax or financing advice
whenYouNeed: From the start of your search, as a deal source
When you respond to a listing or submit an LOI
questions: Who do you represent, and how are you paid?
Why is the owner selling, and why now?
How were the add-backs prepared?
What is the process and timeline, and how many buyers are involved?
Will the seller consider a vendor take-back?

title: Lawyer
summary: Protects your legal position from LOI to closing.
does: Reviews or drafts the LOI and purchase agreement
Leads legal due diligence and registry searches
Advises on share versus asset structure with your CPA
Coordinates closing documents
doesNot: Decide whether the business is a good investment
Replace your accountant on tax and numbers
Run the business after closing
whenYouNeed: Before you sign an LOI
Throughout due diligence
For the purchase agreement and closing
questions: How many small-business acquisitions have you handled in the past few years?
How do you bill: hourly, fixed fee or a mix?
Which parts of the LOI will be binding?
Which representations matter most given our diligence?
What do you need from me, and when?

links.title: Federation of Law Societies of Canada

title: Accountant or CPA
summary: Tests the numbers and plans your tax structure.
does: Reviews financial statements and tax returns
Supports quality-of-earnings and working-capital analysis
Advises on tax structure and price allocation
Sets up bookkeeping and payroll after closing
doesNot: Guarantee the seller's numbers are complete
Give legal advice on contracts
Arrange your financing
whenYouNeed: When you screen serious opportunities
During due diligence
Before agreeing to share or asset structure
questions: Have you worked on acquisitions of businesses this size?
Would you recommend a formal quality-of-earnings review for this deal?
How should we think about share versus asset purchase for tax?
What working-capital level is normal for this business?
What will you need from the seller?

title: Lender or banker
summary: Provides senior debt and tests whether the deal can carry it.
does: Assesses cash flow, your experience and your equity
Offers term loans and lines of credit
May use federal programs such as the CSBFP
Sets loan conditions and covenants
doesNot: Act as your advisor on whether to buy
Approve every deal that meets a formula
Value the business for you
whenYouNeed: Early, to understand what you could borrow
After an LOI, for a formal application
questions: What debt service coverage do you require?
How much equity do you expect from a buyer?
How do you view a vendor take-back, and where must it rank?
Do you lend under the CSBFP, and how would it apply here?
What personal guarantees will you ask for?

links.title: BDC Business Purchase or Transfer Loan

title: Business valuator
summary: Gives an independent opinion of value when the stakes or disagreement are high.
does: Prepares a valuation report with stated assumptions
Analyzes earnings, risk and comparable transactions
Can support a lender or settle a disagreement on price
doesNot: Set the price you must pay
Replace due diligence
Negotiate for you
whenYouNeed: For larger or complex deals
When buyer and seller disagree on value
When a lender or partner asks for one
questions: What type of report do you recommend, and what does it cost?
Which approaches will you use?
What information do you need?
How long will it take?

title: Insurance advisor
summary: Makes sure the business and you are protected from the day you take over.
does: Reviews existing coverage
Recommends property, liability and other commercial coverage
Advises on key-person and life insurance a lender may require
doesNot: Cover known problems you did not disclose
Replace legal protections in the purchase agreement
whenYouNeed: During due diligence
Before closing, so coverage starts on day one
questions: Is the current coverage adequate for this business?
What claims history should I know about?
What will a lender require?
What gaps do you see?

title: Mentor
summary: An experienced owner or operator who helps you think clearly.
does: Challenges your thesis and assumptions
Shares what went wrong in their own deals
Acts as a sounding board during the transition
doesNot: Make decisions for you
Replace professional advice
whenYouNeed: From the start of your search
Before big decisions
In the first 100 days
questions: What do you wish you had known before you bought?
What do you see as my biggest blind spot?
How often can we talk?

title: Settlement and newcomer-business programs
summary: Free and low-cost services that help newcomers settle and build a business network in Canada.
does: Help with settlement needs, such as language classes and credential guidance
Offer business workshops and networking for newcomers
Connect you with local mentors and programs
doesNot: Give immigration advice unless they are licensed to
Finance an acquisition themselves (usually)
Replace your lawyer or accountant
whenYouNeed: As soon as you arrive
When building your Canadian network and credit
questions: Which services do I qualify for?
Do you run business or entrepreneurship programs?
Can you introduce me to local owners or mentors?
